messages.content: Write the charter for a newly formed platform engineering team. Around 250 words.

# Platform Engineering Team Charter

## Purpose

We build and run the internal systems other engineering teams depend on: CI, deployment, runtime environments, observability, and the connections between them. Our customers are the engineers at this company. We measure ourselves by their throughput, not by our own output.

## What we own

- Build and release tooling, from commit to production.
- The runtime platform: compute, networking, secrets, and the defaults that ship with them.
- Developer environments and the local-to-production feedback loop.
- Observability plumbing (metrics, logs, traces) and the alert routing built on it.

## What we do not own

Product code, product on-call, and business logic. When a service breaks because of its own bug, we help debug it. We do not take the page.

## How we work

**Paved paths, not gates.** A team can go off the path. It then carries the operational weight itself.

**Self-service first.** If the same request reaches us as a ticket twice, the third time it is an API or a command.

**The platform is a product.** It has a roadmap, users we talk to every week, and deprecations announced with a migration path and a date attached.

## How we know it is working

Time from merge to production. Time for a new engineer to ship their first change. Change failure rate. Manual tickets absorbed per week, trending down.

## Decisions

Technical direction is set by the team, in writing, in ADRs. Anything that changes another team's daily workflow gets a two-week comment window before it ships.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

# Platform Engineering Team Charter

## Why we exist

We build and operate the internal systems every other engineering team relies on: CI, deployment, runtime, observability, and the wiring between them. Our users are the engineers here. Our success shows up in their throughput, not in our own ticket count.

## What we own

- Build and release tooling, from commit through production.
- The runtime platform: compute, networking, secrets, and the defaults they ship with.
- Developer environments, and the loop between a laptop and production.
- Observability plumbing (metrics, logs, traces) and the alerting routed on top of it.

## What we don't own

Product code, product on-call, business logic. If a service falls over because of its own bug, we will sit with you and debug it. The page still goes to you.

## How we work

**Paved paths, not gates.** Any team can step off the path. That team then carries the operational weight.

**Self-service first.** When the same request arrives as a ticket twice, the third one is an API or a command.

**The platform is a product.** It gets a roadmap, users we talk to weekly, and deprecations that arrive with a migration path and a date on them.

## How we'll know it works

Merge-to-production time. Days until a new engineer ships their first change. Change failure rate. Manual tickets absorbed per week, and that number falling.

## Decisions

The team sets technical direction, in writing, in ADRs. Anything that changes another team's day gets two weeks of comment before it ships.
